🚨 WARREN BUFFETT ISSUES BLUNT WARNING TO NVIDIA CEO JENSEN HUANG OVER AI SPENDING FRENZY 

Warren Buffett, in a rare direct critique, challenged $NVDA CEO Jensen Huang's expansive vision by stating that while the AI boom is transformative, "vision without financial discipline can become a very expensive mistake." 

Buffett contrasted the current market frenzy with the fundamental principle of durable value, implying that building infrastructure purely on hope rather than tangible, long-term earnings capacity risks significant capital destruction when the inevitable cycle turns.

Addressing the astronomical valuations and massive capital expenditures fueling the AI revolution, Buffett warned that the greatest danger to investors is overpaying for growth, no matter how promising the technology appears. 

He suggested that the competitive moat claimed by many AI-adjacent companies is often illusory and that many players will eventually find themselves trapped in a commoditized race to the bottom, unable to justify the immense upfront costs required today.

Buffett concluded by reaffirming his belief that true business success isn't measured by technological hype or quarterly revenue spikes, but by the consistent, sustainable generation of free cash flow that provides a solid return on invested capital. 

He cautioned against the "fear of missing out" that drives executives and investors alike to chase the next big thing without rigorous financial analysis, declaring that history is littered with companies that had brilliant visions but failed because they could not make the math work.
